advisory.finding: On a bug close, the caused_by edge is written via `_write_link_event`, which explicitly performs no idempotency check, and `process_link` appends a dep entry per LINK event with no dedup. A reopened bug that is re-closed (or repeated explicit `--caused-by` with the same id) will accumulate DUPLICATE `caused_by` edges to the same culprit.
merged_from: An explicit `--caused-by <id>` that does not resolve to an existing ticket is not rejected: `resolve_ticket_id(culprit, tracker) or culprit` falls back to the raw user string, and the edge is then written to that unresolved id, creating a dangling caused_by link.
scenarios: A bug is closed (edge drawn), reopened, then re-closed — a second identical caused_by edge is appended
A user re-runs close with the same --caused-by id after a reopen
advisory.suggested_fix: In _apply_caused_by, consult `rebar.graph._links._is_active_link(ticket_id, culprit, "caused_by", tracker_dir)` and return early if it already exists, mirroring add_dependency's idempotency guard.

dropped.finding: test_user_guide_has_blame_hunt_advisory is a prose change-detector, not a structural-boundary assertion. It greps docs/user-guide.md for the substring 'caused-by'/'caused_by' anywhere in the lowercased text; no non-human consumer parses that token, so it merely guards the author's wording and breaks on a behavior-preserving reword/reorg of the doc.
scenarios: Rewording the advisory (e.g. describing it without the literal token) with no behavior change would fail the test.
